scope: Prepare a generic independently developed OS-agnostic C++17 JSON5/strict-JSON library for compatible hosted and embedded projects. Errors are explicit results, never thrown. Schema/CLI/editor remain optional. Agents may prepare CMake, GoogleTest, docs, requirements and skills; no production C++.
requirement_status: Draft; creating issues does not promote proposal requirements to Agreed or establish implementation evidence.
quality_scope: Automated quality checks are unit tests and formatting only. Deterministic grammar, schema, failure-injection and adapter cases may run as unit tests. Do not add fuzzing, sanitizers, e2e, integration-test, benchmark, target deployment or separate differential-test jobs.
license: Retain the existing Apache-2.0 repository license. MIT in the source proposal is a proposed choice, not authorization to change the current license. Preserve third-party notices and pinned provenance.
adaptations: The latest user scope replaces WSL/AdaptivePi SDK/runtime/deployment obligations with a generic portable C++17 library for compatible projects.

J5-083 through J5-090 describe an optional reference profile/example, isolated from the core, rather than a required AdaptivePi infrastructure integration. Preserve consumer-policy separation and traceability to the original proposal; recheck consumer-owned assumptions before describing that example as compatible.
J5-091 is adapted to native Windows/Linux/macOS compiler portability and portable cross-compilation support, without mandating a particular ARM64 SDK or deployment path.
J5-092/J5-093 retain reusable packaging and immutable dependency/source versions without introducing AdaptivePi dependencies.
J5-095 external fixture evidence is implemented through pinned representative fixture unit tests only; automatic differential/reference-tool jobs are superseded.
J5-097 fuzzing and sanitizer evidence is deferred; deterministic boundary, truncation, transformation and regression unit cases remain in scope.
J5-098 allocation/limit/cancellation failure injection remains an in-process unit-test responsibility.
J5-082 installed VS Code and Remote SSH end-to-end acceptance is deferred; language-service components and host/runtime fixture parity receive unit tests.

J5-099 the original Yocto/QEMU, sanitizer and installed-consumer integration matrix is superseded; document compatible native C++17 toolchains and run the selected unit tests in supported exception configurations.
J5-100 measured footprint/throughput benchmarking is deferred; release documentation must describe only implemented and unit-tested capabilities.
New J5-101 records the explicit OS-agnostic embedded requirement. Host unit evidence is not target certification or proof of a embedded runtime integration.

MICROSAR is an example only. OS independence and compilation into compatible embedded projects are the requirement; no dedicated vendor port, SDK or workflow is needed. All library errors shall use non-throwing explicit outcomes even in an exception-enabled consumer.

milestones.title: 1. Portable foundations
milestones.description: Settle draft contracts, portable C++17 targets, Apache-2.0 provenance and unit-test/formatting workflow.

milestones.title: 2. JSON5 and strict JSON reader
milestones.description: Implement complete grammar, owned values, exact numbers and precise recoverable errors.

milestones.title: 3. Resource and failure contracts
milestones.description: Recoverable allocation, explicit limits, bounded work, reusable contexts and deterministic semantics.

milestones.title: 4. Optional Draft-07 validator
milestones.description: Implement an independently buildable offline schema component with exact assertion/reference semantics.

milestones.title: 5. Host CLI and VS Code
milestones.description: Provide usable diagnostics, offline schema assistance and incomplete-document editing through optional host components.

milestones.title: 6. Optional consumer example
milestones.description: Demonstrate externally applied profile/schema policy without coupling the generic library to an application.

milestones.title: 7. Portable packaging and release
milestones.description: Publish reusable CMake targets, supported compiler documentation and truthful unit-test traceability.

issues.title: Define the public C++17 API and draft behavior contracts
issues.goal: Define reviewed C++17 public API contracts and types for explicit bytes/length, syntax defaults, results, ownership, exact numbers, errors and allocation before a developer implements the production reader. Agent work is documentation and planned GoogleTest cases only; production C++ belongs to the developer. All library errors use non-throwing explicit outcomes in every supported compiler exception mode.
acceptance: Public headers use portable standard C++17 and expose no AdaptivePi, WSL, host-tool or editor types.

Document exact-length/read-only/non-NUL-terminated input semantics and mode/result defaults; add API/configuration GoogleTest cases as the corresponding declarations become available. Complete parse behavior is verified by subsequent grammar issues.

Specify that syntax, conversion/access, allocation and limit errors return explicit outcomes and never throw in any supported build; exception-enabled consumers use the same API. Invalid input must not assert or abort. Complete runtime cases land with the implemented reader.
Document syntax defaults, ownership/views, duplicate policy, conversions, error categories, limits and thread-safety; unresolved choices remain Draft.
notes: Compatible C++17 projects are the supported goal; do not promise every historical C++ implementation.

issues.title: Add portable component builds, unit-test tooling and dependency provenance
issues.goal: Provide CMake 3.25 configuration for independently selectable parser, schema, host tools and tests, with a minimal parser build and unit-test/formatting workflow. Retain Apache-2.0 and track licensed dependencies, data and fixtures.
acceptance: Parser-only configuration does not enable schema, CLI, editor or tests implicitly and requires no network access.
Compiler settings are target-scoped and portable across selected MSVC, GCC and Clang C++17 environments.
Provide documented commands and CI checks only for unit tests and formatting; no fuzz, sanitizer, integration, end-to-end or benchmark jobs.
License and provenance files retain Apache-2.0 and list pinned incorporated source/data/fixtures with their upstream notices.
notes: The proposal's MIT suggestion does not override the existing Apache-2.0 license.

issues.title: Implement UTF-8 validation, Unicode whitespace and BOM policy
issues.goal: Establish documented reproducible Unicode data and validate every source byte in both modes, including comments and trailing trivia. Implement mode-specific whitespace and the explicit strict-JSON leading-BOM option.
acceptance: Unit cases reject overlong UTF-8, encoded surrogates, invalid/truncated sequences and values beyond U+10FFFF at token, comment and trailing positions.
Unit cases cover JSON whitespace, JSON5 named/Zs spaces and BOM at leading/interior boundaries; strict JSON ignores at most one leading BOM only when configured.
Record table Unicode version, provenance and reproducible generation/vendor process; representative historical and newer property memberships do not depend on process locale.

issues.title: Implement comments and object/array punctuation in both modes
issues.goal: Implement JSON5 comment placement/termination and container punctuation, including the single JSON5 trailing comma while strict JSON rejects extensions.
acceptance: Unit cases cover EOF line comments, all line endings, unterminated block comments, attempted nesting and quoted comment delimiters.
Empty/nested containers and a single trailing comma parse as specified; holes, doubled commas, missing separators and misplaced colons fail at precise token locations.
Run each discriminating fixture in both syntax modes.

issues.title: Implement lossless quoted strings, escapes and continuations
issues.goal: Decode JSON and complete JSON5 string grammar into a lossless representation, preserving escaped UTF-16 units and distinguishing checked Unicode export from parse acceptance.
acceptance: Unit cases cover quoting, raw controls, forbidden raw CR/LF, truncation, every JSON escape and JSON5 x/v/zero/non-escape behavior; a/e decode as letters and forbidden digit escapes fail.
LF, CR, CRLF, U+2028 and U+2029 continuations join content correctly; raw separators preserve content and produce nonfatal JSON5 warnings.
Paired/unpaired surrogate units and pair order are preserved without substitution; valid raw non-BMP characters agree with paired escapes.
Fixtures assert exact decoded units/lengths and locations, with strict-mode distinctions.

issues.title: Implement Unicode IdentifierName keys and escaped identifiers
issues.goal: Implement the referenced JSON5 IdentifierName grammar with reserved words, Unicode positional properties and decoded identifier escapes; strict JSON continues to require quoted keys.
acceptance: Unit fixtures cover dollar/underscore, reserved-word names, non-ASCII letters, combining continuation marks and ZWNJ/ZWJ.
Digit-first names, unrelated punctuation and escapes decoding to illegal start/continuation characters fail.
Quoted, bare and escaped spellings yield the same decoded key where equivalent; strict mode rejects unquoted names.

issues.title: Implement strict/JSON5 number tokens, literals and token boundaries
issues.goal: Recognize exact grammar spellings and complete boundaries for numbers and primitive literals without eager floating-point conversion or case folding.
acceptance: Strict-number units cover integer/fraction/exponent forms and reject leading plus/zeros, missing digits, hex and nonfinite literals.
JSON5-number units cover signed decimal/hex, leading/trailing decimal points, exponents, NaN/Infinity and reject octal/binary/separators/malformed signs/case.
Lowercase true/false/null parse; lookalikes and unknown identifiers in value position fail.
Boundary fixtures such as truex, 1foo, 0x1z and trivia inserted inside a token fail instead of accepting prefixes; huge finite tokens remain syntax-valid within limits.

issues.title: Complete the reader and maintain a grammar coverage matrix
issues.goal: Connect token and structural parsing so exactly one root of any valid type is consumed, followed only by permitted trivia, and trace every JSON5/strict-JSON grammar production to unit tests.
acceptance: Unit cases cover primitive/container roots, trailing permitted comments, empty/whitespace/comment-only input, additional roots and junk after a valid prefix.
Grammar matrix includes Unicode, malformed and representative every-byte truncation cases with decoded-value/location assertions and cross-mode expectations.
Document remaining grammar gaps and prevent a full-support claim until all productions are covered.

issues.title: Implement the owned value model and checked access
issues.goal: Provide owned distinct value types, length-aware strings/names, ordered arrays and every source object member, with checked access and explicit lifetimes in a pure in-memory API.
acceptance: Unit cases distinguish null/absent, boolean/number and all value categories; wrong-type, missing-member, ambiguous duplicate lookup and out-of-range index return explicit outcomes.
Empty/NUL content and repeated object members remain observable; array/member source order is preserved.
Destroy/overwrite input and move documents before inspecting values/names/tokens; views follow documented lifetime rules.
Checked UTF-8 export succeeds for valid pairs and fails explicitly for unpaired units, without substitution.
The core has no filesystem, process, environment-expansion or network dependencies.
notes: Storage design can start with I01; complete acceptance follows the reader. Numeric conversion and duplicate policies are supplied by the next issues.

issues.title: Implement decoded-key equality and selectable duplicate policy
issues.goal: Use exact decoded key content, without normalization/case folding, for generic preserve-all and explicit reject-duplicates behavior. Report both colliding source occurrences.
acceptance: Unit cases cover bare/quoted/escaped collisions at root and nested objects; equal names in separate objects do not collide.
Generic default preserves all duplicates; configured rejection returns no successful document and reports both occurrences.
Differing case and canonically equivalent differently encoded keys remain distinct; injected hash collisions cannot replace equality checks.

issues.title: Implement exact numbers and checked numeric conversions
issues.goal: Own original numeric tokens and exact finite mathematical information, expose integrality separately from lexical spelling, and provide explicit checked integer/floating conversion outcomes.
acceptance: Unit cases preserve spellings around 2^53, signed/unsigned limits, long integers/fractions, huge exponents and overflowing hex tokens.
Integer conversions report wrong type/nonintegral/out of range without rounding/wrapping; include 0x10000000000000001, bounds/adjacent values and negative unsigned inputs.
1, 1.0, 1e0, 0x1, +1 and close fractions distinguish value and spelling without a double intermediary.
Floating conversion documents rounding/overflow/underflow and remains locale independent without mutating exact storage.
Negative zero and explicit signed Infinity/NaN remain distinguishable from finite conversion overflow; strict mode rejects nonfinite syntax.

issues.title: Implement structured diagnostics, source spans and minimal failure reporting
issues.goal: Retain original byte spans and stable structured error categories with documented line/column conventions, including allocation-free fallback code/location reporting.
acceptance: Unit cases distinguish syntax, encoding, duplicate, access, numeric, configured-limit and allocation errors without parsing prose.
Check exact offsets/ranges for LF/CR/CRLF, Unicode separators, multibyte text, escaped strings, duplicate occurrences, invalid UTF-8 and end-of-input.
Moved documents retain spans after input destruction; any retained source ownership/cost is explicit and configurable.
An exhausted allocator still yields a usable minimal stable error code/location if rich messages or pointer construction fail.

issues.title: Implement recoverable allocation and atomic reusable contexts
issues.goal: Route library-controlled allocations through a fallible mechanism and ensure every failed operation releases temporary resources, publishes no success/partial document and leaves contexts reusable.
acceptance: In-process allocation-injection units fail each reachable allocation in representative success/failure paths, including owned-result and diagnostic construction.
Allocation accounting shows no leaked temporary blocks; retained success-result storage and allocator lifetimes are documented.
Alternate valid, malformed and allocation-failing operations in one context and assert unambiguous success/error results in both exception modes.
Audit containers/dependencies so unsupported throw/abort-on-OOM paths are not advertised as recoverable.

issues.title: Implement configurable limits, bounded traversal and cancellation
issues.goal: Validate and account for named input/storage/diagnostic/work budgets across parse, conversion, comparison and cleanup, with explicit cancellation or deterministic work exhaustion.
acceptance: Unit cases exercise below/equal/above boundaries for bytes, depth, nodes/members, decoded units, numeric token/exponent size, owned bytes and diagnostics.
Invalid option combinations and checked arithmetic overflow fail before processing; no truncation can manufacture success.
Deep partial construction/destruction, adversarial duplicate sets and large numbers stay within checked stack/work budgets.
Cancellation at multiple work boundaries yields distinct operational outcomes and bounded cleanup; document calibrated defaults and accounting.

issues.title: Implement deterministic semantics and independent concurrent contexts
issues.goal: Remove shared mutable global state and hidden locale/environment options, defining independent parser/document concurrency and immutable-schema use with separate work contexts.
acceptance: Unit cases concurrently run independent valid/failing parser contexts and repeat equivalent input/options/version results.
Changed supported locales and environment settings cannot alter values or primary error categories; decimal parsing still follows the grammar.
Document unsupported sharing of mutable contexts and add equivalent immutable-schema concurrent units when schema lifetime support lands.

issues.title: Establish the optional Draft-07 component and schema compilation
issues.goal: Select/implement a separately buildable Draft-07 engine that preserves core precision/exception/resource contracts, explicitly reports its dialect and compiles strict-JSON boolean/object schemas against a vendored meta-schema.
acceptance: Unit cases cover true/false schemas, invalid roots, wrong keyword shapes, malformed patterns and unsupported dialect requests.
Record the Draft-07 meta-schema URI, immutable revision and notices; compilation needs no live download.
Parser-only targets expose no schema dependencies; schema dependencies and supported exception/allocation paths are inventoried.
Maintain an explicit required-keyword coverage matrix, with unsupported work recorded until later issues complete it.

issues.title: Implement offline URI/reference resolution and recursive schema semantics
issues.goal: Compile references through an explicit registry/resolver with Draft-07 URI scopes, JSON Pointers and ref-sibling semantics, supporting progressing recursion and rejecting nonprogressing cycles/resource exhaustion.
acceptance: Unit registry fixtures cover nested IDs, relative/absolute references, escaped pointers, fragments and registered external schemas without network retrieval.
Unresolved references have distinct outcomes; ref assertion siblings are ignored as Draft-07 requires.
Recursive list/tree cases progress through instances; reference-only cycles and exhausted budgets return operational errors rather than hanging or fabricated assertion failures.

issues.title: Implement the required Draft-07 assertion vocabulary
issues.goal: Implement all required type, number, string, array, object, composition and conditional assertions with nested/interacting and nonapplicable-type behavior; numerical/equality/regex precision is completed by the following issues.
acceptance: Unit fixtures cover type/type arrays, enum/const; multipleOf and all bounds; length/pattern; items/tuple/additionalItems/min/max/uniqueItems/contains.
Object fixtures cover properties/patternProperties/additionalProperties/required/propertyNames/min/maxProperties and property/schema dependencies.
Composition fixtures cover allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not and if/then/else including branches, interactions and nonapplicable types.
Required keyword matrix links positive/negative/boundary units; no required assertion may be silently skipped or relabelled optional.

issues.title: Implement exact schema numeric semantics and deep equality
issues.goal: Use exact finite mathematical values for integer/bounds/multipleOf and type-aware deep equality for const/enum/uniqueItems, with explicit schema-instance rejection of duplicate members and nonfinite numbers.
acceptance: Unit cases compare 1/1.0/1e0/0x1, 1e-1, large/close values, negative zero and exact decimal multipleOf without floating rounding.
Explicit NaN/Infinity fail at the instance boundary rather than as invalid parser syntax.
Deep equality respects type, order-sensitive arrays and order-independent uniquely named objects; booleans never equal numbers.
Duplicate-member instances receive their own boundary outcome, and nested/reordered object/array fixtures exercise enum/const/uniqueItems.

issues.title: Implement Unicode schema string lengths and bounded regex semantics
issues.goal: Count Unicode characters rather than UTF-8 bytes and provide documented Draft-07-compatible pattern/property-name matching with explicit invalid/unsupported patterns and Unicode-instance outcomes.
acceptance: Unit cases cover astral/combining characters, decoded escapes and NUL for lengths and property names.
Anchored/unanchored and interoperable required regex fixtures follow the documented dialect; invalid or unsupported patterns produce structured compilation/operational outcomes.
Unpaired surrogate instances never pass through replacement decoding; regex work has a documented budget mechanism.

issues.title: Implement schema metadata, extensions and optional assertion capabilities
issues.goal: Retain applicable schema annotations for tooling without mutating instances, follow Draft-07 unknown-keyword handling and expose format/content assertions only through explicit supported capabilities.
acceptance: Unit cases verify instance equality before/after validation and no insertion/conversion from defaults/examples.
Metadata includes title/description/default/examples/readOnly/writeOnly/comment with references/branches and no misleading inactive defaults.
Unknown schema keywords do not become assertions and remain distinct from unknown instance fields; optional typo warnings are nonassertive.
Baseline format/contentEncoding/contentMediaType remain annotations; requested unsupported assertion modes return explicit errors, and advertised options have units.

issues.title: Implement structured schema outcomes and source-aware assertion diagnostics
issues.goal: Distinguish validation/assertion/schema/reference/unsupported/operational outcomes and emit bounded fail-fast/collect-all diagnostics with instance pointers, schema URI/locations, keywords and source spans.
acceptance: Unit cases distinguish every outcome and diagnostic-count boundary; an assertion failure followed by allocation/cancellation failure cannot hide the operational error.
Nested arrays and slash/tilde/empty/Unicode names use correct RFC 6901 escaping.
Externally registered reference failures identify the originating schema URI/keyword, and instance pointers map to original source bytes where available.
Minimal allocation-free reporting remains usable when diagnostic paths or text cannot be built.

issues.title: Implement bounded schema evaluation, owned compiled graphs and pure validation
issues.goal: Account for schema reference/branch/equality/regex/error work and own compiled reference graphs independently of temporary input/registry buffers. Validation uses separate work contexts and performs no external operations.
acceptance: Unit cases bound branch-heavy schemas, repeated references, expensive patterns, deep uniqueItems, cancellation and injected allocation failures, checking cleanup.
Destroy registry/input temporaries and move/reuse compiled schemas before validation; document any explicitly retained resolver lifetime.
Independent concurrent work-context units share immutable compiled schemas safely.
Fakes demonstrate validation performs no network/filesystem/process/environment-expansion calls; external loading occurs only at explicit compilation/resolution boundaries.

issues.title: Implement the validation CLI and versioned machine diagnostics
issues.goal: Build an optional portable host CLI for file/stdin validation with explicit syntax/schema/profile/limit choices and readable plus versioned strict-JSON diagnostic/capability output.
acceptance: Unit-test command parsing, bounded reader abstractions and execution with fake I/O: 0 valid, 1 input/assertion/profile invalid, 2 configuration/I/O/operational failure.
Cover malformed input, invalid schemas, unreadable-file fake, unsupported options, limits and cancellation.
Machine output round-trips through strict-JSON units and escapes arbitrary Unicode/control content; include locations/pointers/severity/version/capabilities and minimal OOM output.
Package CLI separately so library users and cross-compiled targets require no host-tool runtime.

issues.title: Package VS Code support with workspace-local offline schema associations
issues.goal: Provide a reproducible extension or compatible documented setup with an explicit language ID, supported VS Code versions and local schemas selected by workspace file patterns, including multiple roots and offline operation.
acceptance: Unit-test association/configuration resolution for two roots, relative local references and file patterns; do not insert schema metadata into instance documents.
Unit fakes confirm local completion/validation needs no background network fetch; optional remote loading requires explicit configuration and runtime-compatible reference identities.
Document installation, reproducible packaging, supported versions and optional Remote SSH setup without imposing a remote development environment.
Unrelated language associations stay unchanged; host/editor dependencies do not enter core targets.

issues.title: Implement editor grammar parity, byte-to-position mapping and document versions
issues.goal: Align complete-document editor tokenization/diagnostics with both supported grammars, accurately map original source bytes to editor positions and discard cancelled/outdated responses.
acceptance: Language-service units reuse grammar fixtures for Unicode identifiers/whitespace, escapes, continuations, controls and numeric forms with syntax-mode expectations.
Position units cover astral/combining text, CRLF, continued strings, errors before/after multibyte text and valid EOF ranges using the documented protocol encoding.
Mock rapid edits, reopen/schema changes, cancellation and out-of-order backend responses; stale results never replace a newer document version.

issues.title: Implement incomplete-document recovery and schema-aware completion
issues.goal: Provide provisional editing assistance for malformed/incomplete text and context/style-aware schema property/value completion without treating recovered trees as successful runtime parses.
acceptance: Language-service units request assistance inside unfinished objects, arrays, strings and escapes; native parser units reject the same incomplete documents.
Root/nested/referenced/type-union/conditional schemas suggest applicable names and enum/const/example/default values with required-field indicators.
Existing properties suppress ordinary duplicate insertion; quoting and insertion text remain valid for each completion context.
Every recovered tree/result is marked provisional and cannot be returned as a runtime successful document/validation.

issues.title: Implement schema hover, runtime-parity diagnostics and explicit consumer policies
issues.goal: Show relevant descriptions/types/constraints in hover, align editor assertion outcomes with the native validator and keep duplicate/root/Unicode/numeric-spelling policies distinct from generic syntax.
acceptance: Language-service units cover field/enum hover, unknown fields and conditional failures.
Shared fixture units compare editor/native outcomes for 1, 1.0, 1e0, 1e-1, large integers and source ranges.
Generic and explicit consumer profile units distinguish syntax acceptance from root/duplicate/Unicode/spelling rejection; decoded duplicates are errors under reject policy.
No AdaptivePi-specific policy becomes the generic parser or editor default.

issues.title: Add an optional versioned consumer schema and profile example
issues.goal: Demonstrate an isolated external consumer profile using JSON5, object-root and duplicate rejection plus a descriptive strict-JSON Draft-07 schema, using the proposal's AdaptivePi manifest snapshot only as a reference example.
acceptance: Example units show generic primitive/duplicate parsing separately from configured profile rejection.
Compile the vendored version-1 example schema with the local meta-schema and check a complete valid example plus per-field missing/type/null/pattern/bound/conditional failures.
Fixed objects reject unknown fields while dynamic environment names follow their name rule and require string values.
Document local editor association, snapshot revision and all unresolved consumer assumptions; no core application fields, services, filesystem layout or dependency are introduced.
notes: Optional reference example only; the user requested a generic library. Do not claim agreed AdaptivePi compatibility or create AdaptivePi infrastructure work.

issues.title: Document optional profile numeric/string policies and consumer result mapping
issues.goal: Show how a standalone consumer adapter applies lexical integer/string/path policies, preserves arguments and owned data, implements consumer defaults and maps explicit core/schema errors into its own result type.
acceptance: Example units compare mathematical-integral and explicit lexical policies on decimal/exponent/fraction/hex/plus spellings; booleans, true fractions and nonfinite values fail integer fields.
NUL/unpaired-surrogate and lexical traversal fixtures reject at the profile boundary without changing valid bytes or claiming filesystem security checks.
Owned fake-consumer units preserve empty/ordered arguments, derive argv[0] outside the parser and distinguish consumer defaults from schema annotations without mutating parsed data.
Fake result mapping distinguishes malformed/encoding/duplicate/version/field/conversion/resource errors and adds no ara::core/AdaptivePi dependency.
notes: Keep consumer-specific defaults unresolved until separately agreed. Filesystem existence/permissions/symlink containment and service management remain consumer responsibilities.

issues.title: Ensure OS-agnostic integration into embedded projects
issues.goal: Make the generic C++17 core usable on embedded devices after compilation into a compatible consuming project, without requiring an operating system. Document the runtime/storage and generic CMake toolchain boundary. MICROSAR is one example only; no dedicated vendor port, SDK or workflow is required.
acceptance: Document the required C/C++ runtime subset, compiler/runtime support, alignment/byte-order/data-model assumptions, static initialization and bounded stack/work storage.

Core targets require no POSIX/Windows APIs, files/processes/network, OS threads, locale/environment/clock, exception/RTTI runtime, default global heap, GoogleTest or optional host component dependencies.

Support caller-supplied fallible storage and deterministic budgets; GoogleTest units exercise fixed storage, exhaustion/cleanup, no-OS adapters and data-model boundaries as production APIs are implemented.

Provide generic caller-owned CMake toolchain guidance with tests and host components excluded. A consuming project can compile/link the core using its compatible embedded toolchain without a vendor-specific port workflow.

Return errors as explicit non-throwing outcomes in every supported compiler exception mode; document actual embedded support without claiming host units establish every device runtime, real-time guarantees or certification.
notes: Production C++ is implemented by the developer; agents may prepare CMake, GoogleTest and documentation. This adds generic embedded usability to hosted portability, not a dedicated MICROSAR product.

issues.title: Provide portable reusable CMake packages and pinned build metadata
issues.goal: Support generic compatible hosted and embedded C++17 projects with namespaced parser/schema exported targets, add_subdirectory and installed find_package use, offline dependencies and immutable release/build-option records.
acceptance: Document supported native MSVC/GCC/Clang toolchains and standard CMake cross-compilation without imposing WSL, a Yocto SDK, AdaptivePi deployment or ARM64 runtime.
Parser-only and schema-enabled target/package metadata is relocatable, target-scoped and does not alter parent flags, enable tests or implicitly fetch dependencies.
Compile the selected unit-test targets on documented supported compilers; record any known platform/compiler restriction rather than asserting universal implementation support.
Release metadata pins source/dependency revisions and records compatible exception/allocator/ABI-impacting options; host tools/editor remain separate.
notes: J5-091's original application-specific platform requirement is superseded by the user's generic-library direction. No deployment or installed-consumer integration-test job is added.

issues.title: Complete parser grammar, truncation and failure-injection unit coverage
issues.goal: Complete deterministic in-process unit coverage of grammar/value/location/resource contracts, using pinned compatible upstream fixtures and minimized known regressions without introducing broader test categories.
acceptance: Trace each grammar requirement to valid/invalid/truncated cross-mode units that assert exact decoded values/locations; representative tokens are truncated at every byte.

Vendor licensed pinned representative official JSON5/JSONTestSuite cases as unit data, documenting optional-case and duplicate/precision/Unicode/limit semantics instead of adopting reference output blindly.
Fixed whitespace/comment/escape transformation units preserve expected values; deterministic deep/wide/boundary regressions return stable failures without crashes/uncontrolled loops.
In-process units fail each representative parser/conversion/schema/reporting allocation and limit/cancellation boundary in supported exception modes, verifying cleanup/no partial success.
Required checks remain unit tests and formatting.
notes: Automatic differential/reference-tool runs, fuzzing, sanitizers and benchmarking from the source proposal are deferred/superseded by the user's unit-test/formatting scope. Do not claim executed evidence for them.

issues.title: Complete Draft-07 and editor component unit-test traceability
issues.goal: Run pinned required Draft-07 suite fixtures through unit tests with offline registered references, and trace editor service unit coverage for highlighting, live diagnostics, completion, hover, mapping and native parity.
acceptance: Record Draft-07 suite revision, required/optional selection, counts and failures; required assertion/reference cases cannot be silently skipped or reclassified optional.
Offline registry fixtures supply suite references and add exact numeric, Unicode and parser/editor parity regressions missing from upstream cases.
Editor unit fixtures cover all service behaviors with explicit backend/extension compatibility metadata; mock document versions, associations and cancellation.
Coverage records distinguish executed unit evidence from manual/deferred installed-editor/Remote SSH acceptance; screenshots/README claims are not parity evidence.
notes: Installed VS Code, Remote SSH and end-to-end jobs from J5-082 are deferred under the user's current test scope; no other test category is introduced.

issues.title: Document supported builds and complete a truthful release checklist
issues.goal: Publish supported C++17 compiler/exception configurations and release documents covering actual implemented APIs, standards/Unicode versions, matrices, limits, licensing, packaging/editor instructions and known deviations.
acceptance: Record selected supported native compiler/toolchain versions and actual unit-test/formatting results for exceptions-off/on configurations; identify unverified/unsupported combinations explicitly.
Requirement, grammar and schema-keyword matrices link owning issues and implemented unit cases; Draft/Agreed/Implemented/Verified states stay distinct.
Release checklist documents public contracts, dependency/source versions, allocator/ABI options, reproducible packaging, offline use and optional components/example scope.
Do not claim full grammar/schema/editor support while unresolved gaps remain, or claim fuzz/sanitizer/integration/target/deployment/benchmark evidence that was not requested/executed.
Keep original broader verification intentions visible as superseded/deferred and explain the current unit-test/formatting acceptance scope.
Record J5-101 embedded port/runtime status separately from host unit passes; OS-agnostic embedded support must remain a reviewed core capability, not an assumed certification claim.
Parser-only releases are allowed. Schema/editor/CLI prerequisites apply only when those optional components are shipped; optional consumer examples never block a generic core release.
notes: The original Yocto/QEMU/installed-consumer/sanitizer matrix and performance measurement obligations are superseded or deferred. Optional consumer examples may ship separately and are not a dependency for releasing the generic parser.
